narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Drawing Sheet"**

The whole society is one general-arrangement engineering drawing. A 2px ink frame sits inside a margin that carries zone references: column numbers 1 to 8 along the top and bottom edge, zone letters A to F down the left edge, one letter per section. Inside the frame, every region is a ruled view: hairline-divided cells on drafting film, headed by a condensed capital title, a leader line and a circled balloon letter. The page ends where a drawing ends, in a title block: the society name, its purpose, the channel cells and the email cell.

Density is that of a working drawing: many small labelled fields, big uppercase view titles, and real build photos plotted into traced frames. Colour is almost entirely ink on film. Two accent inks do the coding work: blue for the control/Unibot programme, red for the fighting bots, their join actions and every email action. Nothing is lifted, rounded or glowing; depth comes only from ruling and the 2px frame. The world rejects the dark neon combat-robot hero and the full-bleed-photo-under-headline society template.

All copy, links, photos and committee entries come from one file, `content/site.ts`; the page renders entirely from it. A photo set to `null` renders as a section-hatched "Photo to add" view, so missing imagery is drawn honestly rather than faked.
keyCharacteristics: Light drafting-film ground with near-black ink (plus a chalk-on-graphite Night sheet and a seasonal Hallowe'en sheet, cycled from the strip toggle); one 2px frame, everything else 1px hairlines.
An 8-column zone grid that the margin numbers literally label.
Zone letters A–F in the left margin; balloon letters on view titles match the zone they head.
Blue codes Unibot/control; red codes fighting bots and the email action; ink carries the committee application.
Barlow Condensed uppercase for every title and action, Barlow for reading, Azeret Mono for zone markers, specs and captions.
Square corners on every rectangle; circles only for balloons and leader terminals.

One signature motion, the plot: every rule is drawn left to right, then each view's contents ink in, then its coloured actions sweep in. The first viewport plots on load; each later zone plots once as it enters.

rules.name: The Coding Ink Rule
rules.body: Blue means control/Unibot; red means fighting bots or email. A colour is chosen by what the element belongs to, carried through a single `--tone` / `--tone-deep` pair set by `tone-blue` or `tone-red`. Never pick an accent for variety.

rules.name: The Red Email Rule
rules.body: Every email action is a solid red fill with white text. There is no outline or ghost email button, and red fills are not used for anything that is not email or a fighting-bot join action. The committee application is an ink action, never red.

rules.name: The Hatch Is Not Ink Rule
rules.body: Hatch (1.56:1 on film) draws dividers and hatching only; any text uses ink, ink-2 or ink-3.

rules.name: The Lettered Caps Rule
rules.body: Every h1–h3, nav item, button and field label is uppercase Barlow Condensed. Sentence-case is for Barlow reading copy only.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: Azeret Mono carries zones, specs, captions and the email address, never sentences of prose.

rules.name: The Plotted Line Rule
rules.body: Every line on the sheet is a background stroke whose length is the registered `--draw` property (`linear-gradient(colour, colour) left top / var(--draw) 1px no-repeat`), never a `border`. At rest `--draw` is 100%; the plot animates it from 0%. A new line drawn as a border will not plot.

rules.name: The Line Weight Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy of structure is 2px ink, then 1px rule, then 1px hatch. No blur, no lift, no glow.

dos: draw new sections as a zone: a 1px rule top edge, the next zone letter in the left margin, a View Title whose balloon carries the same letter.
build cell layouts as ruled grids (1px gap over `rule`, film cells) on the 8-column zone grid.
colour by programme: `tone-blue` for control/Unibot, `tone-red` for fighting bots; email is always red.
render every string, link and photo from `content/site.ts`, and let a `null` photo fall back to the hatched "Photo to add" view.
caption every photo view with a mono label, and keep imagery to real build and meeting photos.

keep entrance motion to the Plot: left to right, rules → ink → actions, on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, once per zone, gated on `html[data-plot]`, and off under reduced motion. Give a new element a `--d` delay in its zone's sequence rather than a new kind of entrance.
draw any new line as a `--draw` background stroke, not a border (The Plotted Line Rule).
donts: round rectangle corners; circles are reserved for balloons and leader terminals.
use blurred or offset shadows for depth; box-shadow is allowed only as zero-blur 1px rulings.
set text in `hatch`, or any text lighter than `ink-3` on film.
use solid red or blue fills for surfaces or decoration; solid tone fills belong to email and join actions (blue also marks text selection), and the committee application is ink.
add neon glow or set a headline over a full-bleed photo; the night sheet is the same drawing in chalk, not a combat-arena look.
use glyph or icon-font arrows; use the inline stroked SVG arrow.
